requirement_text.REQ-455:
Approved by the user on 2026-10-06. Process design gaps are found late,
in UAT: 35 files under docs/issues/ mention a dead end, an unreachable
step or a missing default route (recent: ISS-0928 no_matching_edge on a
service task in kyc-routing, ISS-0929). Letflow.Definitions.Graph
already checks a good deal (violation codes at
lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex:207-234: missing start or end node,
dangling edge, isolated node, cycle without gateway, missing role,
missing edge condition, multiple default edges,
human_task_no_fallback_edge and more). This entry adds only what is
missing, as deterministic checks that run wherever the existing ones
run, so they do not depend on any model.

FIRST STEP (CODE-DESIGNER): for each candidate check below, establish
by reading graph.ex, semantic_validation.ex and their tests whether it
already exists, exists partly, or is missing, and record the finding
with file and line. Build only the missing part.

CANDIDATE CHECKS:
1. Reachability: every node is reachable from the start node, and from
every node at least one end node is reachable. (check_isolated_nodes
looks at a node's own edges; establish whether a connected island or a
trap with no way out is caught.)
2. Decision without a default route: an exclusive gateway, and any
other node kind whose outgoing edges all carry conditions (ISS-0928
was a service task), has no is_default edge, so an instance can stop
with no matching route. Establish which node kinds can have
conditional outgoing edges and cover all of them.
3. Data used before it is collected: an edge condition or form
expression reads a variable that no form, service output or
sub-process output on ANY path from the start to that point can have
set. Reuse the declared-fields machinery of SemanticValidation; report
only the case where no path sets it (certain), not the case where some
path does not (that is a judgment for PROCESS-AUDITOR, REQ-456).
4. Unbound task roles at install: when a definition or solution pack is
installed or activated in a tenant, every role a human task routes to
that has no tenant_role binding in that tenant is listed. Decision
0029 section 2 keeps required roles advisory and role seeding out of
packs; do not change that. This is a reported warning in the
validation result and the install response, never a silent pass and
never an automatic binding.
New findings in 1 to 3 are violations (activation is refused, same as
the existing codes). State in the design whether any definition
shipped in priv/ or seeded by scripts/ fails a new check; if one does,
report it to ORCH as an issue with the definition and node named, and
do not weaken the check.
OPEN QUESTIONS: - "A definition already active in a tenant that fails a new check keeps running. Default: new checks apply at validate, activate and import time only; nothing is deactivated."

task.description: WF-02 step 01 (CODE-DESIGNER): produce lib/letflow/design/req455-definition-validator-gaps.md. Local-only run: do NOT push, commit nothing (ORCH commits). Read first: docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md (INV-1..INV-10; state whether any route/permission/response shape is touched, esp. check 4's 'install response'), docs/anti-patterns.md (grep relevant entries; it is 330KB), docs/migration/decisions/0029 (section 2), lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (violation codes ~207-234), semantic_validation.ex, solution_pack_install.ex, export_import.ex, and their tests under test/. For EACH of the 4 candidate checks, classify exists / partly exists / missing with file:line evidence (FIRST STEP in requirement). Keep diff surgical: open PRs #2254 (REQ-444: login_discovery, config/runtime.exs, docs/requirements.yaml, status v26/index), #2228, #2249 (ci.yml); other worktrees touch login_directory/identity/routers. List every file to touch. No implementation code bodies. Do not edit docs/requirements.yaml. Use scoped mix runs with a unique MIX_TEST_PARTITION (e.g. 41); RAM is tight.
acceptance_criteria: the design lists each candidate check as exists, partly exists or missing, with file and line evidence, and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-verifies each classification

for each check that was built: one test with a minimal definition that violates only that check and asserts the new violation code and the offending node or edge id, and one test showing a valid neighbour case passes
the ISS-0928 shape (a service task with only conditional outgoing edges and no default) is rejected at validation, with a test

every process definition shipped in the repository or seeded by scripts/ is run through the validator in a test; each failure is either fixed in the same change or filed as an issue and named in the run report
mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, mix test and mix letflow.check_boundaries pass, real output quoted

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req455-definition-validator-gaps.md. Classification: check 1 (reachability from start / path to end) MISSING; check 2 (default route) PARTLY EXISTS (HUMAN_TASK = CHK-19; EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY missing; conditional edges on service/timer/sub-process already refused by CHK-14); check 3 PARTLY EXISTS (REQ-372 undeclared-variable on gateway edges only; form expressions already same-form scoped); check 4 MISSING. Plan: new Graph.validate_flow/1 (CHK-22 :unreachable_node, CHK-23 :no_path_to_end, CHK-24 :no_default_route) wired into create/update/validate/activate; data-flow class inside SemanticValidation.validate/2 (:variable_never_collected); new Letflow.Definitions.RoleBinding with warnings appended to existing install warnings list and an additive warnings key on the validate 200 body. Probes (mix run --no-start, dev) confirmed classifications empirically. 12 shipped graphs pass existing validators; 11 of 12 would fail CHK-24 (gateways without default); design fixes them in-change following ISS-0928 precedent and asks ORCH to file one BA-owned issue for the proposed default targets.

issues.description: 11 of 12 shipped process definitions have EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY nodes with no is_default edge and would fail new CHK-24: QA meridian_loan_origination v1.3 (eligibility-gate, authority-routing); meridian_regulatory_compliance_review v1.3 (severity-routing, post-remediation-check); swiftroute v1.1 (ceo-approval-gate); vortex_production_order_release v1.1 (budget-gate); vortex_supplier_quality_deviation v1.2 (false-positive-check, severity-routing); simulation yaml meridian/process_claim_intake (kyc-routing, eligibility-gate, authority-routing), meridian/process_policy_binding (severity-routing, post-remediation-check), swiftroute/process_route_approval (ceo-approval-gate), swiftroute/process_shipment_dispatch (injury-check), vortex/process_quality_check (budget-gate), vortex/process_work_order (false-positive-check, severity-routing). Design fixes them in the same change with proposed default targets; ORCH to file one BA-owned issue to confirm the business routing.

Requirement text says ISS-0928 was a service task; ISS-0928.yaml records an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY (kyc-routing) with no default. The literal service-task-with-only-conditional-edges shape is already rejected by CHK-14 :unexpected_edge_condition. Design tests both shapes.

Modules.Installs.install/3 discards the pack install result, so check-4 warnings do not reach the module-install response; existing role_mapping_checklist.bound compares against static platform roles, not tenant_role rows. Both reported, not changed.
